abstract: We study maximin share (MMS) allocations of $m$ indivisible items among $n$ agents with additive valuations. We prove that for both goods and chores, the optimal MMS approximation factor converges to $1$ as $n$ grows. In particular, for every fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, sufficiently large $n$, and any $m$, we give polynomial-time algorithms that compute a $(1-\varepsilon)$-MMS allocation for goods and a $(1+\varepsilon)$-MMS allocation for chores. Furthermore, both algorithms can be implemented using a polynomial number of bundle comparisons.
